summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with inoperable cholangiocarcinoma and a history of recurrent biliary infections, was admitted for fever (101.3°F) following a routine percutaneous biliary drain (PTBD) exchange. He was afebrile upon arrival and remained so throughout hospitalization. Initial labs showed mild pancytopenia, which stabilized, and liver enzymes were within baseline. Blood cultures remained negative, and ultrasound showed no new biliary obstruction or abscess. The fever was attributed to transient bacteremia post-procedure. Constipation with tarry stools was noted, but no acute gastrointestinal bleed was evident. He was managed with a short course of IV meropenem, then transitioned back to home suppressive Bactrim. Apixaban was held due to prior thrombocytopenia, with recommendation to discuss restart with oncology. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned.
